en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Turning Back, 38. The Training Rule on Foreign Countries.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were wandering on tour without a caravan through a foreign country considered risky and dangerous.
Thugs raped them.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [as before] ...were indignant, complained, and spread it about, saying:
“How indeed can nuns wander on tour outside the kingdom where it is considered dangerous and perilous, without a caravan? … [The Buddha asked:
“Is it true, monks, that nuns are wandering on tour outside the kingdom where it is considered dangerous and perilous, without a caravan?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How indeed, monks, can these bhikkhunīs go on tour outside the kingdom where it is considered dangerous and perilous, without a caravan?
This, monks, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of the faith of those who have it…” [and so forth].
And furthermore, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule thus:
“Whichever nun should travel on tour without a caravan through a foreign country that is considered dangerous and fearful, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya). Whichever nun...
[the rest follows].
Whichever [nun] of such a kind... "a nun" ...pe...
this is the nun intended in this context.
“Tiroraṭṭha” means in another kingdom, excluding that kingdom in whose domain he dwells.
“Sāsaṅka” (perilous) means:
On that road, the place where the bandits had encamped is seen; the place where they had eaten is seen; the place where they had stood is seen; the place where they had sat is seen;
the place where they had lain down is seen. That road is called "perilous" because people are seen there who have been killed by the bandits, plundered, and beaten.
"Without a caravan" means without a company of travelers.
"He should go on a journey" means... [he should wander].
In a village where a cock can fly from one house to another, there is an offense of *pācittiya* for every interval between houses.
In a forest area where there are no villages, there is an offense of *pācittiya* for every half-yojana traveled.
There is no offense—
He travels with a caravan,
he travels in safety and without fear,
and in times of calamity.
"Against one who is insane," "against one who is a first-offender.
The eighth training rule is concluded.
